# Intake Brief — Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old

## Problem statement

AI_Hell's enemy roster (E1–E7) is a coherent but self-contained set of
formations. It does not yet deliberately mine the **classic arcade era** for
signature, instantly-recognisable enemy behaviours. This epic researches that
era and turns the best candidates into implementable work items, so the game
can grow a distinctive "arcade homage" roster without ad-hoc, un-scoped enemy
requests.

## Users

- **As the game designer**, I want a researched, curated catalogue of classic
  arcade enemy behaviours adapted to AI_Hell's neon-vector rules, so that new
  enemy work starts from a clear design brief rather than a one-line wish.
- **As an implementing agent/developer**, I want each selected enemy to have
  its own work item with a user story, testable ACs, predicted key files and a
  plan that follows the existing data-driven enemy convention, so I can
  implement it without re-deriving the design.
- **As the producer**, I want the candidates that were considered but not
  selected recorded, so the roster can be expanded later without redoing the
  research.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A research document `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` exists and catalogues at least 5 and at most 8 selected classic arcade enemy archetypes, recording for each its source game, original behaviour, adaptation to AI_Hell's neon-vector code-drawn no-enemy-collision rules, and why it was selected.
- The research document includes a considered but not selected section listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- One child work item exists per selected archetype, each containing a user story, measurable and testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and a plan that follows section 8.6 Adding a new enemy in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and each child references this epic and the research document.
- Each selected archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven pipeline, whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and give its enemy difficulty scoring inputs for movement, fire and health factors.
- Each selected archetype's notes name the gym scenes that will exercise it, existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym, to satisfy the gym-to-game parity rule.
- Validation checks the research document recommendations against existing engine constraints so every selected archetype maps to an existing or explicitly-planned formation/shot-pattern registry entry, and every child work item carries explicit unit-test acceptance criteria.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** — no external art assets
  (GDD §7.2).
- **Gym↔game parity** — an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a
  gym and the game; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`. Enforced by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs
  assertion (AGENTS.md).
- **Data-driven enemies** — tuning is data, not code; archetypes are rows in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN). A genuinely new entity is
  only justified when the existing formation/shot registries cannot express it.
- **"Enemies are the bullets" design** (GDD §2.4) and **no enemy–enemy
  collisions** (GDD §2.6).
- **Behaviours must be adaptable to a top-down free-2D arena** — the original
  arcade games are lane/axis-based; the brief must state how each archetype is
  translated (or note where translation is not faithful).
- **Scope is research + design + child-item creation.** This epic does not
  itself implement the enemies; each selected archetype's implementation is its
  own child work item.

## Existing state

- **Enemy catalog** (GDD §4.1, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1):
  E1 Scout, E2 Diver, E3 Tank, E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, E6 Asteroid, E7 Harvester,
  plus the multi-phase Boss.
- **Enemy implementation guide** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  documents the shared core scene library, the CSV pipeline (§8), and the
  "adding a new enemy" checklist (§8.6).
- **Data-driven pipeline**: `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`, `src/core/configTypes.ts`,
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`,
  `src/utils/enemyShotPatterns.ts`, `src/utils/formations.ts`.
- **Difficulty scoring**: `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` (absolute 0–100 index;
  movement/fire/health factors), pinned by
  `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.
- **Gym surface**: single reusable `GymEnemies` scene + `GymIndex`; new CSV rows
  appear automatically.
- **Precedent**: E6 Asteroid (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) is already an arcade homage
  built as a non-formation roamer with a split helper — a model for how far a
  new archetype may depart from the formation model.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" already anticipates "Levels 6–10+ with new enemy
  types".

## Desired change

Produce researched, ready-to-implement enemy concepts drawn from classic arcade
games and capture each as a scoped child work item, with a shared research
document acting as the catalogue and the record of deferred candidates.

**Proposed candidate pool** (research selects 5–8; the rest go in the
"considered but not selected" section):

- Space Invaders — marching row that steps left/right and drops bombs.
- Galaga — entrance dive-in formation and tractor/capture beam.
- Pac-Man — ghost chase with distinct pursue/ambush personalities.
- Centipede — segmented chain that descends and reacts on segment destruction.
- Defender — fast attacker with a defined patrol/attack run.
- Missile Command — incoming falling projectiles / orbital strike telegraphed.
- Robotron 2084 — aggressive horde that swarm-steers toward the player.
- Frogger — lane traffic hazard crossing the arena (non-shooting obstacle).
- Joust — flapping momentum-based flyer in the top-down arena.
- Dig Dug — burrower that creates/changes traversal hazards.
- Q*bert — diagonal hopper with a fixed stepping pattern.
- Star Castle — concentric rotating ring shielding a core.

*(Every candidate in the pool is recorded in the research document; only 5–8
become child work items.)*

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` — New. The catalogue of selected and
  deferred archetypes (the epic's primary deliverable).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Updated. Add a reference to the
  research doc; each implemented archetype later updates the catalog (§1) via
  its child item.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Updated. Reference the research doc from
  §4.1 / §8 so the roster direction is traceable.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Updated (by child items, not this epic). New
  rows for archetypes expressible as data.
- `src/entities/<Name>.ts` — New (by child items). Only for archetypes needing
  new entity code (e.g. burrower, segmented chain).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` / new gym scene — Exercised by child items for
  parity.

## Related work

- **Enemy Design tooling** (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN) — completed; the data-driven
  CSV pipeline new enemies plug into.
- **Asteroids as an enemy** (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) — completed; precedent for a
  classic-arcade-inspired, non-formation enemy.
- **Enemy difficulty scoring** (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K) — completed; every new
  archetype must supply its scoring inputs.
- **Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies** (AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52)
  — completed; the `BaseEnemy` seam new archetypes extend.
- **Data-driven enemy health config** (AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR) — completed.
- **Docs and README for enemy config pipeline** (AH-0MTHG5K6O008BCNJ) —
  completed.
- **Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide**
  (AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6) — completed; the guide §8.6 governs each child.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) —
  completed; automated playtests must survive any new enemy, so its behaviours
  are a useful validation input for selected archetypes.
- **Alternative player control** (AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD) — completed.
- **Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments**
  (AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY) — completed; docs-update conventions to follow.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** – Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns (completed)
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** – Alternative player control (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: classic, create, drawn, dropping, eats (+23 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: arcade, classic, create, drawn, dropping (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: create, enemies, epic, era, etc (+17 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the research could expand indefinitely. Mitigation — cap
  selection at 5–8 this round; record all other candidates in the deferred
  section. Extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Fidelity risk**: lane/axis-based arcade behaviours may need significant
  translation to the top-down free-2D arena; the brief requires each archetype
  to state its translation, and permits a documented divergence (per gym-parity
  rule).
- **Pipeline-fit risk**: some archetypes (burrower, segmented chain) cannot be
  expressed as a CSV row alone; the brief requires each to state whether a new
  entity/factory seam is needed before implementation starts.
- **Assumption**: the operator-supplied exemplars (Space Invaders row,
  Pac-Man ghosts, Centipede) are illustrative examples, not a required final
  selection.
- **Assumption**: "classic arcade era" means the coin-op era of the late 1970s
  to mid-1980s.
- **Assumption**: this epic's children implement the enemies; no separate
  implementation epic is needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "How many enemy concepts should this epic research and turn into work
  items?" — Answer (operator): **(A) focused set of ~5–8** from a named
  shortlist of classics. Source: interactive reply. Research: reviewed
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.6 and the existing 7-archetype
  roster; a 5–8 cap keeps the epic tractable and each child implementable.
- Q2 "Should the epic also produce a written research/design document, or only
  the child work items?" — Answer (operator): **(B) a dedicated research doc
  plus child work items**, and *"be sure to include other candidates not
  selected but considered so we can expand the range later"*. Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/intake` step 7
  and the repo's `docs/` convention; no existing research doc.
- Q3 "What should each per-enemy child work item include?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) research + design + implementation of one enemy (full lifecycle in one
  child)**. Source: interactive reply.


---

## Plan

**Breakdown (created as child work items):** 1 research/validation child (R1)
+ 8 archetype full-lifecycle children (one per selected archetype) + 1
docs-integration child (D1). The epic itself does not implement the enemies.

**Selected archetypes (8):**

1. Space Invaders — stepping march formation.
2. Galaga — tractor/capture beam.
3. Pac-Man — ghost personalities (chase/ambush/flank/wander).
4. Centipede — segmented chain that splits on segment death.
5. Robotron 2084 — homing horde that swarm-steers to the player.
6. Defender — patrol-then-attack raider state machine.
7. Missile Command — telegraphed orbital strike.
8. Frogger — non-shooting lane traffic hazard.

**Considered but not selected (recorded in the research doc):** Joust, Dig Dug,
Q*bert, Star Castle.

**Test-first ordering:** R1 (research doc + automated engine-constraint
validation test) → E1–E8 (each a vertical slice: code + tests + code comments +
gym parity) → D1 (cross-cutting docs integration).

**Dependencies:** each archetype child depends on R1 (design brief must exist
before implementation); D1 depends on all archetype children (the GDD catalog
and guide must reflect the implemented roster).

**Phasing (vertical slices):** R1 is docs + validation test; each E* cuts
through the full layer stack (CSV/config → entity/factory/fire seam → shared
core → game + gym parity → tests → code comments); D1 is a cross-cutting docs
slice. Between phases, the next child's description is re-checked against what
was actually delivered and updated before implementation starts.

**Reused seams:** `BaseEnemy`, `EnemyConfig`/CSV pipeline
(`configStore`/`configCsvPlugin`), `formations.ts`, `enemyShotPatterns.ts`,
`enemyFire.ts` dispatcher, `AsteroidSpawner`/`HarvesterSpawner` (non-formation
spawner precedent), `GymEnemies`/`GymIndex`, `enemyDifficulty.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (planning)

- Q4 "When does the archetype selection get fixed?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) fix the 5–8 selection now and create all children in this planning
  pass**. Source: interactive reply. Research: the epic's AC3 requires a child
  per selected archetype and the research doc's content is the same design
  brief, so fixing the set now avoids an extra planning pass and satisfies
  coverage immediately.
- Q5 "Which archetypes do you want selected?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) select all 8 recommended** (Space Invaders, Galaga, Pac-Man,
  Centipede, Robotron 2084, Defender, Missile Command, Frogger); Joust, Dig
  Dug, Q*bert and Star Castle are deferred to the "considered but not selected"
  section. Source: interactive reply. Research: each selected archetype maps to
  a distinct existing/planned engine seam; the deferred four are weaker fits
  for a terrain-less top-down arena or overlap existing entities.
- Q6 "Breakdown shape for the children." — Answer (operator): **(A) a
  test/verification-first research-doc child (with an automated engine-
  constraint validation test) + one full-lifecycle child per selected
  archetype + a docs-integration child**. Source: interactive reply. Research:
  epic AC7 (README/GDD/guide) is cross-cutting and would otherwise be
  duplicated across 8 archetype children.
